The Commonwealth can be hazardous to your health. You can restore lost health through a variety of methods.  Stimpaks restore 30% of your total health over several seconds. Stimpaks also heal all damaged limbs by 30%. Certain perks can increase the amount of health Stimpaks restore.  Many foods restore small amounts of health, but most food will also cause radiation damage, reducing your maximum health. You can restore health lost to radiation damage by visiting a doctor or taking RadAway.  Most settlements also have a resident doctor, who can fully restore your health and damaged limbs for a fee.  Sleeping also fully restores any lost health and limb damage.

Food fills your Hunger meter (if you're human) and also restores lost Health.  However, most food in Appalachia causes radiation damage, reducing your maximum Health. Food will also turn rotten over time if it's not consumed. Uncooked food can also cause Disease.  Food prepared at a Cooking Station eliminates the chance of catching Disease, reduces radiation damage, and typically boosts how well it fills the Hunger meter and how much Health it restores.

To favorite an item, press [Pipboy] to open the Pip-Boy, and then go to Items. Select the item you'd like to favorite and press [RShoulder]. Weapons, Armor, Apparel, Food/Drink, and Aid items can all be favorited.  Press [QuickkeyUp] to access the Favorites menu. Select an item using [Look] and press [Accept] to use the item. Weapons and Armor will be equipped, while Aid items will be consumed.  You can continue to move while the Favorites menu is up. Press [Cancel] at any time to leave the menu.   To remove a favorited item from the menu, open the Pip-Boy and select the item you wish to remove, then press [RShoulder].

The Favorites menu is a way to quickly access items and gear.  To favorite an item, press [Pipboy] to open the Pip-Boy, and then go to Items. Select the item you'd like to favorite and press [RShoulder]. Weapons, Armor, Apparel, Food/Drink, and Aid items can all be favorited.  Move the mouse wheel to access the Favorites menu. Continue to move the wheel up or down to select an item, then [Click] to use the item. Weapons and Armor will be equipped, while Aid items will be consumed.  You can also access your favorites by using [Quickkeys]. Stimpaks are auto-assigned to [Quickkey12]. The first item you favorite is assigned to [Quickkey1], then [Quickkey2], and so on.  You can continue to move while the Favorites menu is up. Press [ForceClose] at any time to leave the menu.   To remove a favorited item from the menu, open the Pip-Boy and select the item you wish to remove, then press [RShoulder].

Fast Travel allows you to quickly move to your Teammates, your Friends, your C.A.M.P., or return to any location you've previously discovered.  To Fast Travel, press [Map] to open the Map. Select a Teammate, a Friend, your C.A.M.P., or a location with [Click], then select "Fast Travel."  Fast Traveling to a location costs a number of Caps based on how far away the location is from you. The further away you're traveling, the more Caps you'll need to pay. Traveling to a Teammate, Friend, your C.A.M.P., Foundation, Fort Atlas, The Crater, The Rose Room, The Rusty Pick, The Whitespring Resort, Dark Hollow Manor, Radiant Hills, Highway Town, Fisherman's Rest or Vault 76 is always free regardless of distance.  You cannot Fast Travel while you are in combat, if you are carrying too much weight, or if you're taking any form of Health damage.

Carry Weight represents how much you can haul in your inventory before it starts to slow you down. The more Strength you have, the more you can carry.  Each item you pick up has a Weight value. If the total Weight of all your items exceeds your Carry Weight, you start to suffer penalties:  - You will not be able to Fast Travel.  - Your Action Points (AP) will drain when you move and you won't be able to Sprint. AP will regenerate whenever you stand still.  - When you run out of AP, you will be forced to move at walking speed. You can move at full speed again when you recover enough AP.  The fastest way to reduce your inventory Weight is to drop items.  To drop an item, press [Pipboy] to enter the Pip-Boy and navigate to the Items tab with [LTrigger]/[RTrigger].  Highlight the item(s) you wish to drop using [LeftStick] and press [XButton].  Items you drop will appear in the world inside a Paper Bag. Other players can loot this bag, and the bag will disappear over time.  If you want to increase your Carry Weight or reduce the Weight of items:  - Choose Strength when you level up to increase your total Carry Weight.  - Wear a suit of Power Armor. The suit will increase your Strength as long as you're in it.  - Equip Perks like Thru-Hiker or Packin' Light to reduce the Weight of certain items.  - Consume items that temporarily raise Strength, like Buffout.  - Store excess items in a secure container, like your Stash Box.

Dogmeat is a special companion who can accompany you as you travel across the Commonwealth.   Like other companions, Dogmeat can aid in combat, carry equipment, and accept commands, but unlike other companions, his opinion of you will not be affected by your actions or decisions. Dogmeat will stick by your side until you dismiss him.  You may only have one companion at any given time.  Combat While Dogmeat cannot use weapons, during combat he will attempt to grapple enemies, holding them in place and making them easier to target. Certain perks provide bonuses when you target grappled enemies.  Companion Menu With a few exceptions, Dogmeat functions just like a standard companion. You can trade items with him, equip him with certain cosmetic gear (bandanas, collars, etc.), and issue commands to him.  For more info on how standard companions work, see the "Companions" entry.  Where Dogmeat differs, however, is the "Talk - [MultiActivateY]" menu. From this menu you can:  - [MultiActivateY] - command Dogmeat to search the area for items - [MultiActivateA] - have Dogmeat perform a trick - [MultiActivateX] - dismiss Dogmeat  When you dismiss Dogmeat, you can tell him to wait for you at any friendly workshop. Otherwise, he'll return to his most recent residence.

Fast Travel allows you to quickly move to your Teammates, your Friends, your C.A.M.P., or return to any location you've previously discovered.  To Fast Travel, press [Map] to open the Map. Move the cursor to a Teammate, a Friend, your C.A.M.P., or a location, press [Accept], then select "Fast Travel."  Fast Traveling to a location costs a number of Caps based on how far away the location is from you. The further away you're traveling, the more Caps you'll need to pay.  Traveling to a Teammate, Friend, your C.A.M.P., Foundation, Fort Atlas, The Crater, The Rose Room, The Rusty Pick, The Whitespring Resort, Dark Hollow Manor, Radiant Hills, Highway Town, Fisherman's Rest or Vault 76 is always free regardless of distance.  You cannot Fast Travel while you are in combat, if you are carrying too much weight, or if you're taking any form of Health damage.

To pickpocket, press [Sneak] and approach your target. When you're within range, press [Activate] to look through their inventory.  Select an item in your target's inventory with [LeftStick] to see your chance to successfully steal it. Press [Accept] to attempt to take it.   If you're feeling particularly bold, press [XButton] to attempt to take everything they have on them.  If you are detected while attempting to pickpocket, your target and any witnesses will immediately become hostile to you.  Note that looking through your target's inventory is not a crime. You will only be attacked if you attempt to steal something and fail. You cannot pickpocket while in combat.  You can also use pickpocket to plant items on your target by selecting an item in your own inventory and pressing [Accept]. Once you've acquired certain perks, you can even plant live grenades or mines on your target, leading to explosive results.  Improve your chances to successfully pickpocket by increasing your Agility attribute or by taking certain perks.

Your settlements require a variety of resources to function: food, water, shelter. If all your citizens' needs are met, it will increase the settlement's Happiness.  The higher a settlement's overall Happiness, the more productive your settlers will be. If Happiness goes too low, you may lose control of a settlement.  The workshop interface displays the current Happiness of your settlement. It can go up or down depending on what resources are available for the settlers who live there.  The basics that each settler requires to be happy are:  Beds Each settler needs a bed: a bed under a roof is even better. The interface will show BEDS in red if there isn't currently one bed for each settler.  Food and Water Each settler needs one food and one water per day to be happy. This food and water can come from current production, resources stored in the workshop's inventory, or from other workshop settlements linked with Supply Lines (see the "Workshop - Settlements" entry for more info on supply lines).  Defense The higher your settlement's overall defense value, the happier your settlers will be.  Some objects actually produce Happiness. This contributes to the total Happiness of the settlement. Settlers can also become unhappy due to events such as Raider attacks, kidnappings, etc.  Note that Happiness, unlike other reported values, doesn't change instantly; it moves up or down over time, based on the current state of the settlement. So if you provide needed food and water to an unhappy settlement, you won't see the Happiness rating change immediately, but you will see it increase over time.   In the same way, if, for example, a Raider attack destroys all of a settlement's crops or water supplies, they won't become instantly unhappy. You'll have time to correct the problem before your settlers become dangerously unhappy.

Many building objects require Power to function. To provide Power to an object, you'll need to hook it up to an existing generator or build a new one from the Building menu in the Generators tab.  Power is shared between most objects by wires. You can run a wire between two objects by switching to the Modify mode by pressing [Pipboy]. Highlight one of the objects and press [YButton] to run the wire.   Objects that are within range of the wire will be highlighted in white. Highlight one of them and press [YButton] again and the two objects will now be connected by a wire.  All objects that are connected together by wires are considered a "power grid," and can use all Power produced within the connected grid. This means you can hook up multiple generators into a power grid in order to provide Power to everything on the grid.  The direction of the wires doesn't matter; Power can flow freely around the grid as long as there is some wired connection between the generator and the object that needs Power.  Highlighting a generator will also highlight all objects that are part of its power grid. Highlighting an object that requires Power will also show if it is currently powered; if the "Requires Power" icon is red, then the object isn't currently receiving Power.   This means that either the object isn't hooked up to a power source at all, or that the power grid that it is attached to is overloaded; there isn't enough power on the grid to supply all the objects that need it.  Wires have a limited range; if you need to run wires a long distance, build objects from the Power Connectors tab to bridge the gap. These include switched versions, which allow you to turn power on and off to anything connected to the switch.  Some objects, such as lightbulbs, receive Power simply from being near a power connector, like a Power Pylon, rather than using a direct wired connection.

Certain workshop objects won't function without someone to work them, and that requires workers.   Some workshops will already have workers available when you gain access to them. To attract new workers to your workshop, build a Recruitment Radio Beacon (Power > Miscellaneous).  To assign a friendly worker to a workshop object, hold [TogglePOV] to enter the Workshop menu, highlight a settler, and press [Activate] to put the settler into Command mode. Then highlight an object (or bed) and press [Activate] again to assign the settler to it.  In some cases, a settler can only work on a single object (stores, for example). However, settlers can work on multiple Food- and Defense-producing objects at once. When you assign a settler to work at a Food or Defense object, they will automatically begin working at any objects without a worker of the same type.  Highlighting a settler will also highlight any objects they are currently assigned to, so you can see what they are currently working on.

The C.A.M.P. (Construction and Assembly Mobile Platform) allows you to build your own corner of Appalachia in any way you see fit.   Setting Up C.A.M.P. Set your C.A.M.P. by opening your Pip-Boy ([Pipboy]) and pressing [LShoulder]. The C.A.M.P. will appear in front of you, highlighted in either blue or red.   If the highlight is blue, then press [Accept] to place your C.A.M.P.  If the highlight is red, the C.A.M.P. cannot be placed here. It might be too close to an existing location or the ground might not be flat enough. Move around until you find a position where the C.A.M.P. turns blue.   Building with the C.A.M.P. Once the C.A.M.P. is placed, walk up and activate it with [Activate], or hold the [TogglePOV] button. You will enter building mode.  In building mode, objects you can build are divided into broad categories. Use [LShoulder]/[RShoulder] to navigate through the categories, then use [Up][Down][Left][Right] to select objects within that category to build. [Left] and [Right] will switch between different variants of the same object, if any.  You can also hold down the [Shift] key and use [W][A][S][D] to select objects and switch between variants instead of using [Up][Down][Left][Right].  After you've selected an object to build, use [W][A][S][D] and mouse move to position the object and [SecondaryAttack]/[PrimaryAttack] to rotate the object's placement. Then press [Accept] to build the object.  You can also hold [Accept] and move the mouse to move the object while staying in place. Hold [Accept] and use the mouse scroll wheel to move the object up and down.   Free Camera Mode  Free Camera Mode allows you more freedom in designing your C.A.M.P. by allowing you to easily move the camera around. You can enter Free Camera Mode by pressing [V].  With Free Camera Mode on, you can press [CTRL] or [ALT] to move up or down.   Attaching Objects Objects can be attached to other objects. For example, a Wall piece can be attached to a Foundation or Floor piece.  To attach two objects, build the first object, then select the second object and move it until it "snaps" into the first object. Then press [Accept] to build.   Creating Buildings A building starts with a Foundation. Go to the Floors category and select one of the Foundations to build. Once you've built a Foundation, you can attach more Foundations to it, increasing the size of your flooring.  You can then attach Walls, Roofs, Stairs, and Doors to the Foundation pieces to create an entire building.  If you want to create buildings with multiple stories, you'll first need to attach a set of Stairs to your Foundation. Then, go to the Floor category and select one of the Floor pieces, then attach them to the top of your stairs to start your second story.   Scrapping and Storing When you Scrap an object in building mode, the object will be removed and you'll receive 50 percent of the components it was built from.  If you Store an object, the object will be removed, but you can build it again later for free. The object will be in the Stored category. Stored objects continue to count towards your build budget. You can scrap any stored items directly from the build menu if you want to clear build budget space.   Benefits of the C.A.M.P. Your C.A.M.P. appears on your map as an icon of your choice. Fast traveling to your C.A.M.P. is always free, regardless of how far away it is from you.  One of the most important items you can build at your C.A.M.P. is the Stash Box. A Stash Box can store a large amount of items and is secure against other Players. Only you can see and access your stash.   Moving your C.A.M.P. You can move your C.A.M.P. to a new location by opening your Pip-Boy ([Pipboy]) and pressing [LShoulder]. When you move your C.A.M.P., anything you built at your old site is packed up and placed in the Stored category in the building mode menu.  When you log out from the game, your C.A.M.P. is packed up. When you log back on, the game will try to set up your C.A.M.P. the way you left it.

Blueprints are a way to group objects together so you can build them again all at once. You can access Blueprints by entering building mode at your C.A.M.P. or a Workshop that you own.   Creating a Blueprint While in building mode, navigate to the Blueprints category and press [XButton] to start creating or modifying a Blueprint.  Select an object you've built by walking up to it and centering it on your screen until it becomes highlighted. Hold [Accept] to add it to the Blueprint.  Add as many objects to the Blueprint as you want. Their position and rotation relevant to each other will all be stored in the Blueprint.  Press [RTrigger] to create the Blueprint.    Select Structure Option The Select Structure option ([LShoulder]) will select every object that is attached to the selected object. Walls are typically attached to foundations and other walls, creating a single structure that the Blueprint can select.   Grow Selection Option The Grow Selection option ([RShoulder]) will attempt to select any objects that are near the selected objects.

Crafting items is done by going to the appropriate workbench/station:  - Armor Workbench: for Armor, Armor Mods, Backpacks, CAMP Pet Clothing, Underarmor, and general Clothing  - Chemistry Station: for Chems and ingredients like Gunpowder or smelted ore  - Cooking Station: for Food, Drinks, and Herbal Remedies  - Power Armor Station: for Power Armor pieces and Power Armor Mods  - Tinker's Workbench: for Ammo, Flamer Fuel, Grenades, Mines, Chests, Fishing, Gifts, Legendary Mods, Quest Items, and Souvenirs  - Weapons Workbench: for Guns, Melee Weapons, and Weapon Mods   Components Crafting an item consumes Components, which are found primarily in Junk items. An old Lantern you find might contain Glass and Steel, for example.  Components are automatically consumed when you craft, destroying the item that held the Components. Anything not used will be refunded to you as raw Components.  If you want to see which Components an item has, Open the Pip-Boy and go to the Items category to see what you're currently carrying. Select an item, and any Components it has will appear next to the description.   Tagging Components for Search When you select an item to craft, Components that you don't have are grayed out. If you press [R3], it will tag the missing Components for search. The Components will have a magnifying glass icon next to them. Whenever you are searching a container, any item that has a Component you have tagged will have the magnifying glass icon next to it.   Storing Junk Items You can store your Junk items quickly using the Stash Box. Approach a Stash Box and press [XButton] to open the Transfer Menu, then [YButton] to Store All Junk.  Any items stored in the Stash Box are available when you're crafting items at a workbench or station.   Scrapping Junk Items You can scrap your Junk items at any crafting station or workbench. Approach the workbench and press [XButton] to open the Scrap Items Menu, then [YButton] to Scrap All Junk.  When you scrap Junk items, you'll receive all the crafting components from them. Components weigh significantly less, so scrapping your Junk items whenever you find a crafting workbench in the world will help you stay under your Carry Weight.   Item Condition Some items, like weapons and armor, degrade as they're used. This is tracked in the Condition bar. When the Condition bar is empty, the item will break.  You can view an item's current Condition by opening the Pip-Boy, going to the Items category, and selecting the specific item.  When you craft an item, the starting Condition of the item is based on your Intelligence.  When you find an item in the world, the starting Condition of the item is based on your Luck.   Repairing Items Repairs to an item can be made at the same workbench/station where you craft the item. Walk up to the workbench and press [YButton] to enter the Modify/Repair menu. If you're already using the workbench, you can switch between the Modify/Repair menu and the Crafting menu by hitting [XButton].   Modifications Armor, Weapons, and Power Armor can all be enhanced with Mods. Walk up to the workbench and press [YButton] to enter the Modify/Repair menu. If you're already using the workbench, you can switch between the Modify/Repair menu and the Crafting menu by hitting [XButton].  Mods occupy a slot on the item, such as the barrel, grip, or sights. While only one Mod can be installed in each slot, you can craft new Mods to replace any existing Mod.   Recipes/Plans Recipes and Plans allow you to craft new items. When you pick up a Recipe or Plan, open your Pip-Boy [Pipboy] and go to Item -> Notes, then activate the Recipe or Plan in order to learn from it. The Recipe or Plan will be consumed in the process.  If you find another copy of the Recipe or Plan, activating it again will do nothing, but it can be traded or sold.   Other Ways of Learning New Crafting Items You can also learn new crafting options when you pick up certain items. The first time you pick up a new raw meat or plant ingredient, for example, you will learn a basic cooking recipe for it. Picking up Gunpowder will teach you how to make more at the Chemistry Station. There are even new decoration options for your C.A.M.P. that you can unlock by picking up signs and other household objects.  Scrapping items, particularly new Weapons, Armor, and Mods that you find while exploring, can also unlock the ability to craft them yourself. Make sure you don't need the item before you scrap it! Try scrapping a piece of Wood Armor or a Pipe Gun Mod you aren't using and see if you've learned how to make it yourself.

Diseases are temporary negative effects that can afflict you after you reach Level 5. You have a chance to catch a Disease when you do any of the following:  - Sleep in a bed that's on the ground.  - Get hit in melee by a Diseased enemy.  - Drink Dirty Water.  - Move through environmental hazards.  - Eat raw food.  - Swim in dirty water.  - Get hit by a trap.  - Move through an area that has bad weather.  The chance to catch a Disease is based on your Endurance. The higher your Endurance, the lower the chance you'll catch any Disease.  You can prevent catching a Disease entirely by:  - Only sleeping in beds that have a frame.  - Avoid getting close to Diseased enemies, so they can't hit you.  - Boiling Dirty Water at a Cooking Station before drinking it.  - Wearing a Hazmat Suit or Gas Mask before moving through environmental hazards.  - Cooking raw food at a Cooking Station before eating it.  - Wearing a Hazmat Suit or Gas Mask before swimming through water.  - Watching out for traps and disarm them before they spring.  - Wearing a Hazmat Suit or Gas Mask if you're outside in bad weather.  If you've caught a Disease, you can open your Pip-Boy [Pipboy] and go to Stat -> Effects to see more information on the penalties you'll be under until the Disease is cured.  Disease Cures and Antibiotics will remove one of the Diseases you're suffering from. Diseases will also expire on their own, given enough time.

Activities:  Activities are public quests that everyone inside their area can participate in, and tend to require a small number of Vault dwellers to complete.  If you wander into an area with an active Activity, you'll receive a notification in the lower-right side of the screen. You'll be added to the Activity if you stay in the area. If you leave the area, you'll receive a similar notification that you'll be removed from the Activity if you don't return.  Any active Activities in the world will also appear on your Map as flashing hexagons. If you select an Activity from the Map, you can fast travel there and join the Activity. Fast Traveling to an Activity costs caps based on your distance traveled. You must not be over encumbered to fast travel to the Activity.  Enclave Activities are public quests run by the secretive Enclave. While anyone can participate in these Activities, members of the Enclave may receive additional rewards.  Everyone inside the Activity area earns rewards when it completes.  Public Events:  Public Events are public quests that everyone inside their area can participate in, and tend to require a significant number of Vault dwellers to complete.  If you wander into an area with an active Public Event, you'll receive a notification in the lower-right side of the screen. You'll be added to the Public Event if you stay in the area. If you leave the area, you'll receive a similar notification that you'll be removed from the Public Event if you don't return.  Any active Public Events in the world will also appear on your Map as flashing hexagons. If you select a Public Event from the Map, you can fast travel there and join the Public Event. Fast Traveling to a Public Event is free, but you must not be not over encumbered.  Everyone inside the Public Event area earns rewards when it completes.

Hunger and Thirst represent how much food or beverage you need to consume to gain bonuses.  The Hunger meter and the Thirst meter appear in the lower-right corner of the screen if you're a human. Hunger is represented by the fork and knife icon. Thirst is represented by the water drop icon. If you do not see either meter, you can open the Pip-Boy to bring them up.  The Hunger and Thirst meters drain over time. They each give out different bonuses depending on how full the meter is:  Hunger Meter - Above 80 percent: you gain +1 Strength, +35 Max HP and +35 Disease Resistance.   - Above 60 percent: you gain +25 Max HP and +25 Disease Resistance.  - Above 40 percent: you gain +15 Max HP and +15 Disease Resistance.  - Above 20 percent: you gain +15 Max HP.    Thirst Meter - Above 80 percent: you gain +1 Endurance, +35 AP Regen and +35 Disease Resistance.   - Above 60 percent: you gain +25 AP Regen and +25 Disease Resistance.  - Above 40 percent: you gain +15 AP Regen and +15 Disease Resistance.  - Above 20 percent: you gain +15 AP Regen.

Leveling up allows you to increase one of your SPECIAL stats, gives you choice of a new Perk, and helps you meet the level requirements for certain equipment.  As you complete quests, defeat enemies, and explore the world, you'll earn Experience Points (XP). Once you've gained sufficient XP, your level will increase.   Open your Pip-Boy and press [YButton]. This will open the Level Up menu. You'll be asked to choose one of your SPECIAL stats to increase. You'll also get to choose a new Perk.  (Note: You will stop receiving SPECIAL increases once your level is higher than 50, but you'll still be able to choose a new Perk.)  After you've made your selections, you'll enter the Perk menu. You can re-assign all your Perks from here. The bottom row of cards are your available Perks, the top row of cards are all the Perks you have equipped.  When you equip a Perk, it is assigned to its associated SPECIAL stat. The Gladiator Perk is a Strength Perk, for example, and goes into your Strength slot when it is equipped.  There is a limit to the number of Perks that each SPECIAL stat can hold. Every Perk has a number in the upper-left corner. This is how many points the Perk is worth. Your total number of Perk points can't exceed the associated SPECIAL stat. For example, if your Strength is 3, then you cannot have more than 3 points worth of Strength Perks. Whether you choose to equip several low point Perks or one high point Perk, is up to you.  You can exit the Perk menu at any time by pressing [Cancel].  You can choose to reallocate your SPECIAL stats by visiting a Punch Card Machine beginning at level 25.  Level Requirements for Items Some Weapons, Armor, and Power Armor pieces have a minimum level requirement to use them. You won't be able to equip an item if you aren't the appropriate level or higher.  You can see the minimum level of an item by going to the Items category in the Pip-Boy and selecting the item.

Mutations give you a mixture of powerful positive and negative effects. Whenever you take Radiation damage, you have a chance to gain a Mutation. You cannot gain Mutations if you are below Level 5.  You can see the effects of any Mutations you have by opening the Pip-Boy and going to Stat -> Effects.  Mutations are semi-permanent. Every time you use RadAway, there is a chance that a Mutation will be removed. You can keep using RadAway for more attempts to remove a Mutation.  Serums are consumable items that will grant a specific Mutation as soon as you use it. If you already have that Mutation, the Serum will temporarily suppress the negative effects of the Mutation.

DESC: PvP (Player versus Player) combat is when two or more Players attack each other. PvP has the following rules:  - Players must be at least Level 5 to engage in PvP.  - When attacking another Player no damage is dealt until both Players have hit each other.  - Once both Players have hit each other they become Hostile to each other. Hostile Players show up as red dots on the compass.  - Teams follow the same PvP rules for determining if a Player is Hostile. Each member of a Team will be determined Hostile individually.   Pacifist Mode  Pacifist Mode is on by default and prevents you from dealing damage to other Players and other Players will always deal reduced damage to you. Messages intended for PvP activity are also turned off.  To turn off Pacifist Mode, press [Map] to open your Map, then [LShoulder] to open the Main Menu. Select "Settings -> Game" and then select Pacifist Mode. You can turn Pacifist Mode off or on at any time.

Workshops are locations in the world that you can temporarily claim and build on. Once you claim a Workshop, you get access to its store of building materials and access to the Workshop's rich resources.   Claiming a Workshop Workshops are claimed by clearing its location of all enemy creatures, then activating the Workshop workbench and paying the Claim cost. A flag will start to rise, indicating your progress. If there are any Hostile Players in the area, they will contest your claim. Drive them out to continue claiming the Workshop.  Once claimed, you can activate the Workshop to start building. See the C.A.M.P. topic for more information on how to use the Building controls.  Your claim to a Workshop is temporary. Hostile Players who enter the location can contest your claim. You'll also lose your claim once you disconnect.   Workshop Resources Every Workshop has resources you can extract by building Collector objects on them, and connecting the Collectors to power. Collectors are found in the Resources category of the Building menu. See the "Power" topic in the Help menu for more information about powering objects.  Collectors will add resources to their inventory over time until they are full, as long as they are operational. However, other Players can steal from a Collector's inventory, so build locks on your Collectors and Turrets to defend them.  Some Collectors can only be built on top of a "hardpoint," which is a specific spot in the Workshop area, such as an Aluminum Deposit or Gravel Pit. If a Collector is valid for that hardpoint, it will "snap" on top of it when you try to place it.  Each Workshop has different available resources, which are indicated on the map. Open the map and move the cursor over the Workshop location to see the list of resources with a number next to each resource. This is the maximum amount of each resource this Workshop will produce every "cycle."   For example, a Water value of 4 means that up to 4 Water Purifiers will produce each cycle. If you have more than 4 Water Purifiers, then the Workshop will randomly pick between the available Water Purifiers and produce at 4 of them. Water Purifiers that aren't powered or whose inventory are full are ignored, so if you had 6 Water Purifiers, but 3 of them were full, then the other 3 Water Purifiers would produce.

Private Teams are groups of Players composed of one Team Leader and 1-3 Teammates.  You can invite another Player to join your Team by walking up to them and pressing [Activate]. You can also invite Players on your Friends list by using the Social Menu, or by selecting them on the Map.  The Player you invite will need to open the Social Menu and select you in order to accept your request.   Social Menu The Social Menu is where you can manage your Friends and your Team.  You can open the Social Menu by opening the Map by pressing [Map] and then pressing [RShoulder].  Use the mouse to navigate the Social Menu. [Click] on the Friends, Team, and Recent tabs to open that list of Players. Then click on a Player to open the options list for that Player, which includes things like inviting them to join your team or adding them to your Friends list.   Team Leader The Player that initially invites other Players to join their Private Team becomes the Team Leader. The Team Leader can kick Players off the Team or promote another Player to be Team Leader instead.  Open the Social Menu and go to the Team category, then click on a Player to open the list of options. You can then select "Kick" and "Promote to Leader" from here.   Perk Sharing You can select a Perk that will be shared to all members of your Team. Enter the Perk Menu, select an equipped Perk, then press [T]. You can only share Perks that have a point value equal to or lower than your Charisma.   Fast Travel You can fast travel to your Team Leader or Teammates for free by selecting them on the Map.   Leave Team You can leave a team by opening the Social Menu, select your profile and then select "Leave Team."

Vendors are typically robots that have been programmed by the previous survivors of Appalachia to sell goods.  When you find a Vendor, they will have a Trade prompt appear when you look at them. Press [XButton] to trade.  In the Trade menu, the list on the left contains your inventory, the list on the right contains all the items the Vendor has for sale. At the bottom of each list are the number of Caps you each have.  Select items in your inventory and press [Accept] in order to sell them. A Vendor that is out of Caps will not be able to purchase your items.  Select items in the Vendor's inventory and press [Accept] in order to buy them. You must have enough Caps to purchase the items, or the transaction will fail.

Trading between Players allows you to buy and sell items from each other for Caps.  Walk up to another Player and press [XButton] to invite them to trade. The other Player will need to look at you and also press [XButton] so that you're both in the Trade menu.  From the Trade menu, you can select items to sell and buy. The list on the left contains your inventory, the list on the right contains the other players inventory. Even if the item is not being offered, you can request to trade for it. You can filter the view to only show active offers by pressing [R3].  When you select an item to sell, you can set how many of that item that the other Player can buy. They will be able to purchase any number of that item up to the quantity you specify.   You will then be asked to set an Item Price. This is the price for each item the other Player purchases. For example, if you set the Item Price to 10, and the other Player buys 2 items, they will pay a total of 20 Caps.

Death occurs whenever your Health drops to zero.  Reviving and Respawning You will drop to the ground and a timer will begin. If another player runs up and revives you before the timer runs out, you will stand back up. Otherwise, you will need to respawn when the timer runs out or if you press the Give Up button.  When you respawn, you will need to pick a location on the Map. Locations far away from you will cost Caps to respawn there, but you will always be able to respawn at a Teammate, Friend, your C.A.M.P., Foundation, Fort Atlas, The Crater, The Rose Room, The Rusty Pick, The Whitespring Resort, Dark Hollow Manor, Radiant Hills, Highway Town, Fisherman's Rest or Vault 76 for free.  The location of your last death will appear on your Map and the Compass as a skull and crossbones icon.   Dropped Loot After you respawn, any Junk Items in your Inventory will be dropped where you died inside a Paper Bag.  You will receive a Miscellaneous Objective pointing to your dropped loot. If nothing was dropped, or you died in a location that is no longer available, you will not receive an objective as there is nothing to retrieve.  Any other Player can grab what you dropped when you die. Your dropped loot can also go away if you log out before retrieving it.

A Stash Box is a special container that safely stores any items you put in it.  Items stored in a Stash Box are accessible from any other Stash Box in the world. Typically, Stash Boxes are built by you at your C.A.M.P., but they can also be found in the world. The Train Stations and Red Rocket stations scattered throughout Appalachia each have a Stash Box.  Each Player can only see their own items in a Stash Box. So while multiple Players might be accessing the same Stash Box in the world, each Player is only seeing, storing, and taking their own items from it.  When crafting objects, any items in your Stash Box can be used for components. This is true for crafting stations and workbenches out in the world, in addition to ones you build at your C.A.M.P.

The denizens of Appalachia can be a talkative bunch. When you interact with select characters, you'll enter Dialogue Mode. While in this mode, you'll be temporarily immobile, but can exit at any time by pressing [Cancel].  Often while in Dialogue Mode, you'll be asked for your input on the matter at hand. These dialogue options will appear as gold text in the center of your screen. If you've selected a dialogue option previously, it'll be gray instead.  To select an option, move your cursor over it and use [Click]. You can also move through the various options using [Up]/[Down].   To adjust your camera while in Dialogue Mode, hold [Mouselook] and move your cursor.  Locked Dialogue Options Not all dialogue options are available to all players. Some options will be preceded by a stat, which could be the name of a S.P.E.C.I.A.L. trait, a Reputation level, or some other relevant criteria. If you don't have the required stat, the dialogue line will appear at the bottom of the list in red (though, in some cases, lines might be hidden from the player).  Conversation History If you'd like to see what's been recently said in your current conversation, you can turn on your Conversation History. While in Dialogue Mode, press [ShowHistory] to toggle the Conversation History window. You can adjust its size in the Display section of the Settings menu.  Team Listening If you're on a team with another player and would like to hear what's going on in their conversation, you can approach your teammate and press [QCBButton]. You'll then be able to listen in on their conversation as it proceeds. If you'd previously enabled your Conversation History, you'll also be able to see you teammate's dialogue choices.

As you travel across Appalachia, you'll build relationships with its occupants - both good and bad. Increasing your Reputation with the factions of Appalachia has some significant advantages, while getting on a faction's bad side can close off opportunities... and even get you killed.  Viewing Your Reputation You can view your Reputation with the factions of Appalachia at any time by visiting the Social Menu and pressing [Up] until you reach the Reputation display.  Reputation Benefits and Costs Having a good Reputation with a group has its benefits, including access to their vendors, Daily Quests, and, as your Reputation increases, the opportunity to purchase better and better equipment.  However, if your Reputation gets too low with a given group, all those benefits disappear: faction vendors cease to sell to you, Daily Quests are no longer available, and members of the faction out in the wilderness may even attack you on sight!  Increasing Reputation There are three primary ways to increase your Reputation with a faction:  - Make choices during your quests that favor that group and its members  - Perform Daily Quests for the faction (which unlock after visiting their home base for the first time)  - Aid members of the faction you encounter out in the Appalachian wilderness  Losing Reputation There is only one major way to lose reputation - siding against the faction during your quests. Other actions may make a faction hostile to you, but only quest decisions will result in permanent reputation loss.  Repairing Reputation If you've significantly damaged your reputation with a faction, you can visit Cherise at the Wayward (after you've finished the Wayward and Main Questlines) to reset your Reputation value with a given faction - for a price.

Allies are permanent residents at your personal C.A.M.P. who can provide you with new activities while also defending your personal space.   You'll encounter potential Allies in your travels across Appalachia. Some will require you to earn their trust; others will jump at the opportunity to join you.  Once you've convinced an Ally to sign up with you, you'll unlock a new workshop item at your C.A.M.P. Building this item will call in the newly acquired Ally, unlocking their gameplay content and providing your C.A.M.P. with a full-time resident.  To remove your Ally from your C.A.M.P., scrap or store your Ally's workshop object, and they'll leave you alone until you rebuild it.  You can only have a single Ally at your C.A.M.P. at a time, so keep that in mind as you acquire additional Allies.

In Wastelanders, select interior spaces are now Instanced. Instanced spaces are personal to each player, allowing them to affect the space based on their own personal choices and actions.  Instanced interiors, however, have a few facets that differentiate them from standard interiors:  - Only the Instance owner and their teammates can enter an Instance. Strangers and non-team friends will be unable to follow players into an Instance.  - Quest progress is saved less frequently inside an Instanced interior. If you're in the middle of a quest in an Instanced space, make sure you wrap up your current activity before logging off.  Teammates and Instances When on a team, a player has two options when it comes to entering an Instance: enter their team leader's Instance  or enter their own personal Instance.  When approaching an Instanced interior that your team leader has already entered, you can press [QCAButton] to enter your team leader's Instance or [QCXButton] to enter your own.  While teammates are in their team leader's Instance, their ability to affect the space is limited. They'll be able to activate objects like doors and buttons and fight enemies, but they'll be restricted from doing the following:  - Teammates cannot activate characters in their team leader's Instance.  - Teammates cannot progress their team leader's quest while in their leader's Instance. Only the team leader can do that.  - Similarly, teammates cannot progress personal quests inside their team leader's Instance. They'll need to exit and enter their own Instance in order to progress personal quest content.  - Teammates cannot remain in their team leader's Instance without them. If the team leader leaves, any teammates will be kicked from the Instance shortly thereafter.

Gold Bullion is a special currency that can be acquired once you've completed your journey through the Wastelanders Main Quest. Collecting and spending Bullion is the only way to unlock the ability to craft some of the best items in the game, so acquiring it should be a priority for players of all types.  Acquiring Gold Bullion You can purchase Gold Bullion directly from Smiley, your friendly neighborhood Bullion dealer at the Wayward (though you'll need to finish the Main Questlines before he'll come to town). Smiley sells up to 300 Bullion per week.  The other way you acquire Bullion is by converting Treasury Notes at Gold Press Machines you can find in Crater and Foundation. You can use the press machine to get up to 400 Gold Bullion per day.  You acquire Treasury Notes as rewards from Wastelanders Daily Quests and all Public Events.   Spending Gold Bullion Four vendors accept Gold Bullion as currency:  - Minerva, who can be found camped at Foundation, The Crater, or Fort Atlus. Her camp moves each week.  - Regs, who can be met by finishing the Wastelanders Main Quest  - Mortimer at The Crater  - Samuel at Foundation

Use left and right on the stick to navigate to the Public Teams tab.  Public Teams are visible to all Players in the world through the Public Teams tab on the Social Menu. Use [Move] to navigate the list of Public Teams and press [Activate] to join one. This will add you to the Public Team if it is not full.  You can also join a Public Team by walking up to the Team Leader and holding [Activate].  You can create a Public Team by selecting the "Create New Team" option in the Public Teams tab. Selecting this option opens a menu to choose a goal for your new Public Team. Use [Move] to navigate the list of goals and press [Activate] to create a new team with the selected goal. There are various goals that each offer a unique bonus to all members of the Public Team. Creating a new Public Team will send a notification to every Player currently in the world, inviting them to join your team.   A Public Team will not appear in your Social Menu if you have blocked its Team Leader or if you have been blocked by its Team Leader. Bonds Your Public Team bonus will increase based on the number of bonds between you and your team members.  Playing with another Player on a Public Team will form a bond with them. When the meter completely fills, you will become bonded to that Player. Bond progress will persist while both Players are still in the same world, even if they leave the team or change teams. Lunchboxes are consumable items that you can open to gain a boost to the Experience Points (XP) you earn as well as one of eight random Buff Effects. Additionally, any player in your vicinity when opening a Lunchbox will also receive the XP Boost as well as one of the possible buff effects. Other players may not get the same effect as you.   XP Boost Each Lunchbox that affects you increases the XP you gain from all sources by 25%. This effect will stack up to 100% total bonus. Any Lunchboxes that affect you when you are at the 100% bonus effect will refresh the effect timer.  The XP Boost lasts for 60 minutes and is paused when you leave the game.   Buff Effects Each Lunchbox applies a buff effect to an affected player in addition to the XP Boost. There are 8 possible effects, and players can only have a single copy of an effect on them at a time; if the player were to receive the same effect, the timer for the effect is refreshed. The Buff effect lasts for 60 minutes and is paused when you leave the game.  Available Buff Effects are: - Gift Bag - Increased Carry Weight. - Confetti Mess - Adds colorful explosions to some creature deaths. - Plastic Animals - Increased damage to Animals. - So Much Cake - Reduce Hunger gain. - Fingertrap - Increased damage to Super Mutant enemies. - Antacids - Increased Radiation resistance. - Noisemaker - Increased damage to Robot enemies.  - To-go Punch - Reduce Thirst gain.  Effect Odds Players have a 100% chance to receive the XP Boost effect from a Lunchbox. Players have a 100% chance to receive a Buff Effect; there is a 12.5% chance to receive a particular Buff Effect from a Lunchbox.  Notes While we currently have no plans to change the odds, we reserve the right to update or modify information shown above at our discretion to reflect changes and/or evolving reporting standards. Lunchboxes are not available for purchase in some territories.  Last Updated: 10/07/2020

Shelters are instanced interiors that act as expansions to your C.A.M.P. Each Shelter has its own workshop budget, which is roughly 1.5x your normal C.A.M.P. budget.   Entrances Shelters are accessed by placing Shelter Entrances in your C.A.M.P.. Once a Shelter entrance is placed it can be used to teleport you into one of your Shelters.You can even place entrances inside Shelters to create a "daisy chain" effect! You can place multiple Shelter entrances of any type, but all entrances of a certain type will lead to the same instance of their associated Shelter. For example, you can place three Vault Atrium Shelter entrances separately, but all three will lead you to the same instance of your Vault Atrium Shelter.  Shelter entrances can be locked and unlocked like regular workshop doors. Locked Shelter entrances can be lock picked like other workshop doors.   Building Building in Shelters may feel different than building in Appalachia does. Some workshop rules have been relaxed or removed. Items will not require support and are allowed to float. The floors in your Shelter also act as foundations, so you can build structures directly on top of them. You can toggle workshop snapping rules on and off in the workshop menu using [ReadyWeapon].  Each Shelter comes with a built in Shelters Control Panel, which you can use to enter workshop mode, Scrap All in your current Shelter, or Repair All in your current Shelter.  Some workshop categories have been blacklisted in Shelters. You cannot build Allies, Food, Water, Resources.  Social Shelters support PVP encounters. If you are hostile to another player on the surface you will retain your PVP status when you enter a Shelter. The inverse is also true - if you become hostile to another player inside a Shelter your hostile status will be retained if you return to the surface. If you die inside a Shelter you will not drop a loot bag.  Shelters also support building in teams. You can build in your teammates' Shelters and they can build in yours.  Paper Map If you or one of your teammates places a Shelter at your C.A.M.P. and leaves it unlocked, you will see a small "Shelters" icon next to that C.A.M.P. on the paper map.

Ultracite Battery Cell Charge, also known as "Ultracell Charge", is an in-game currency that players will use to embark on Expeditions. The Ultracite Battery Cells are depleted and must be recharged before use on the Vertibird which takes you to Expedition locations. Luckily, some folks have what you need to charge them up. For a price, of course.   Acquiring Charge for Ultracite Battery Cells To charge the Ultracite Battery Cells, you will need to complete Refuge Daily quests in and around the Whitespring Refuge. Each Refuge Daily grants a different percentage of charge and will carry over until the Ultracite Battery Cells are used to embark on a Expedition at 100 percent charge.   Ultracite Battery Cell Charge cannot exceed 100 percent and all charge earned after will be wasted.   Acquired Ultracell Charge can be tracked on the paper map in the Expeditions window along with the progress on Refuge Dailies.    Using Ultracite Battery Cell Charge To use the Ultracite Battery Cell Charge, players must open the paper map and navigate to the Expeditions window. Once there, players can choose to embark on an Expedition if their Ultracell Charge is at 100 percent. Once they embark on the Expedition, the Ultracite Battery Cell will be depleted to 0 percent.   Ultracite Battery Cell Charge cannot be used until the player has earned the total 100 percent.

Stamps are a currency exclusively earned through completing Expeditions.  Once earned, Stamps can be used to purchase rewards that would otherwise be randomly granted. Stamps give the player control over what they get so be sure to collect as many as you can!    Acquiring Stamps Stamps are acquired by completing Expedition Missions. Certain mission conditions, such as completing optional objectives or being team leader, can yield additional Stamps at completion. Be thorough in your mission to maximize the amount of Stamps you earn in one go. You can check how many stamps you have saved up by opening the Pip-Boy, selecting Stat, and then selecting Collections.  Spending Stamps Stamps can be only be spent at Giuseppe's Curios in Whitespring Refuge in exchange for exclusive Expedition rewards.

Scout's Banners are consumable items that you can open to gain various buffs that help you in combat: Scout's Call, Scout's Code, and Scout's Courage. Scout's Call is a buff that adds a 5% (max 20%) chance to trigger a Scout's Code buff when you kill an enemy. Scout's Codes are various buffs that are designed to help you keep fighting. Each Scout's Banner applies a random Scout's Code. Scout's Courage is a buff that will automatically revive you with a Stimpak if you are incapacitated, once every 5 minutes.   Opening a Scout's Banner will apply Scout's Call, a random Scout's Code, and Scout's Courage not just to you but any player in your vicinity. Other players may not get the same Scout's Code as you.   Scout's Call: Scout's Call gives a 5 - 20% chance to trigger ALL active Scout's Code buffs when you kill an enemy. Each Scout's Banner that affects you increases the odds of triggering Scout's Code buffs by 5%. This effect will stack up to 20% total trigger chance. Any Scout's Banners that affect you when you are at the 20% bonus effect will refresh the effect timer. Scout's Call lasts for 60 minutes and is paused when you leave the game.   Scout's Code: Each Scout's Banner applies a random Scout's Code to the player. Scout's Codes are effects that get triggered if Scout's Call is triggered on an enemy. There are 5 possible effects, and players can only have a single copy of an effect on them at a time; if the player were to receive the same effect, the timer for the effect is refreshed. The Buff effect lasts for 60 minutes and is paused when you leave the game.   Available Buff Effects are: - Teamwork - Restore 100% AP.  - Survival - Restore 20% HP.  - Innovation - Repair 10% Weapon CND. - Discovery - Highlight enemies for 5s.  - Research - Repair 10% Armor CND.  Scout's Courage:  Scout's Courage gives the player 100% chance to auto-revive when incapacitated. This effect is on a 5 minute cooldown. Any Scout's Banners that affect you when you already have Scout's Courage applied will recast the effect.The Buff effect lasts for 60 minutes and is paused when you leave the game.   Effect Odds: Players have a 100% chance to receive the Scout's Call effect from a Scout Banner. Players have a 100% chance to receive a Scout's Code effect from a Scout Banner; there is a 20% chance to receive a particular Scout's Code from a Scout Banner. Players have a 100% chance to receive the Scout's Courage effect from a Scout Banner.  Notes: While we currently have no plans to change the odds, we reserve the right to update or modify information shown above at our discretion to reflect changes and/or evolving reporting standards. Scout's Banners are not available for purchase in some territories.  Last Updated: 09/01/2022

Re-Rollers are a consumable item that you can use to re-roll a Daily or Weekly challenge.  Re-rolling Challenges Daily or Weekly Challenges can be re-rolled from the Challenges screen. - Players are given one free re-roll per day. This free re-roll can be used on a Daily or Weekly Challenge. FO1st members are granted one extra free re-roll per day. - When a player has used up all of their free re-rolls they are able to use a Re-Roller to make additional re-rolls. Each Re-Roller consumed grants one additional re-roll. - If a challenge is re-rolled any progress already made towards completing that challenge is lost. Not all challenges can be re-rolled: - Completed challenges cannot be re-rolled. - Challenges the player does not have access to cannot be re-rolled (for example, if a player is not a FO1st member they will be unable to re-roll FO1st challenges).  Effect Odds - When a challenge is re-rolled a new challenge will be selected at random. - When re-rolling a challenge players have a 25% chance of the new challenge being an Epic Challenge. Epic Challenges are more difficult to complete and are worth more S.C.O.R.E. XP than a regular challenge.  Notes While we currently have no plans to change the odds, we reserve the right to update or modify information shown above at our discretion to reflect changes and/or evolving reporting standards. Re-Rollers are not available for purchase in some territories.

Punchcard Machine The Punchcard Machine is a C.A.M.P. item. The recipe for this is learned automatically upon reaching Level 25 and can be crafted in the workshop Build Menu. Place the Punchcard Machine on a flat surface within your C.A.M.P. and interact with it to view the Loadouts Menu. Punchcard Machines can also be found at train stations across the world.   Loadout Slots You can purchase additional Slots from the Atomic Shop and purchasing an additional slot is account wide, so any additional slots that you purchase will be available to all characters on your account.   Unallocated Points Players with a loudout that has unallocated S.P.E.C.I.A.L. will automatically go to the Edit SPECIAL screen when first switching to the loadout. They are free to cancel this operation and continue with unallocated points if they choose.   Switching Loadouts SPECIAL Point allocations are easily switched within the Punchcard Machine menu by highlighting the Loadout Slot you wish to load in and selecting it.   Ranking Up Cards Ranking up a card that is in use by multiple loadouts will display a message if any of those loadouts can no longer support the card's new rank value. In some cases, you may want to have the same cards with different ranks to assist in properly setting up additional loadouts.   Scrapping Cards Attempting to scrap a card used by multiple loadouts will display a message warning you that the card will be removed from all loadouts. If confirmed, the card will be scrapped and removed from all loadouts.

The Brown House served as the woodland retreat of the 31st President of the United States, Herbert Hoover and his wife Lou from 1929 to 1933.  This residential cabin's nickname is a nod to the President's more famous residence in Washington, D.C.

Lou Hoover wrote detailed records describing how they would bring beef hearts from a Washington market to feed the trout each evening. It became a favorite daily ritual for the President and First Lady.

President Hoover was an avid fisherman, and his love of the sport helped inspire the selection of this site along the Rapidan River. The Trout Pond was constructed by U.S. Marines so that he could display the fish he caught during his time at the camp.

Each new Season offers a collection of themed rewards that are available to be claimed only for the duration of the Season. Complete in-game activities to earn S.C.O.R.E. and Rank Up. Each Rank earned grants you Tickets that you can redeem to claim Season Rewards.   Complete Challenges to earn S.C.O.R.E. Earn S.C.O.R.E. by completing Challenges. Challenges are given daily and weekly and require completing a variety of in-game activities such as killing certain types of creatures or finding and collecting items in the world.   Ranking Up When you accumulate enough S.C.O.R.E. you will Rank Up. Each new Rank you earn grants you 25 Tickets.  It is also possible to purchase Ranks for 150 Atoms per Rank up to Rank 150.  You can continue to earn S.C.O.R.E. and Rank Up beyond Rank 100.   Redeem Tickets to claim Season Rewards  The Tickets you earn from ranking up can be redeemed for rewards on the Seasons screen.  Access the Seasons screen from the Main Menu or from within game by pressing [Map] to open your Map, then [LShoulder] to open the Main Menu and selecting "Seasons".  Seasons Rewards are listed across multiple pages with each page containing several rewards. Access to the first page of rewards is automatic. A Access additional pages by Ranking Up to the required Season Rank.  You can claim any available rewards by redeeming the required number of Tickets. The Tickets required for each Season Reward vary, with smaller rewards typically requiring fewer Tickets than larger rewards. Occasionally rewards may require 0 Tickets and are free to claim as soon as the page is unlocked.   Fallout First Season Rewards The Fallout First Season Rewards for a particular Season are only available to players with an active Fallout 1st subscription during the relevant Season or players that have purchased the specific Fallout First Season Pass. To claim these rewards you must also have access to the page they are on and have enough Tickets to redeem the reward.   End of Season A Season Pass will apply to a specific Season and will expire at the end of that Season. Rewards and Season Rank are unique to the specific Season and therefore, when a Season ends, any unclaimed Rewards will no longer be available and a player's Season Rank progress and Ticket balance accumulated in one Season will not carry onto the next Season.

If a Weapon or Armor has a star after its name... it's Legendary!  These can be found by defeating creatures with stars in their names (Legendary Creatures!) You can also receive these as rewards for Quests or Public Events, sold by other players, or by crafting one yourself.  At their respective Workbenches, random Legendary Mods can be attached to Armor, Power Armor and Weapons. Items with lower star values can also have additional Mods added to them without disrupting the existing Mods.  If you want to further customize your Legendary Weapon, you can swap out any of it's Mods with another... assuming you've got a loose Legendary Mod, that is.  To craft Legendary Mods, head to the Tinkerer's workbench. You'll need to know the Recipe for the Mod, and have a heap of Legendary Particles to boot.  Particles and Recipes can both be found by scrapping Legendary Weapons, Armor and Power Armor at any workbench. You'll always receive Particles, and in rare cases, you'll learn the Recipe of one of the Legendary Mods attached to the item you scrapped. If you're lucky, you may even get a loose Mod that can be attached right away!  Each time a Legendary Mod is replaced on a Legendary Item, the cost in Legendary Modules will gradually increase.  Modules can be obtained using Scrip. Scrip is obtained by trading Legendary Item the Scrip Machine at all train stations.  Once a Legendary Mod has been replaced on a Legendary Armor, Power Armor or, on a Weapon, that Legendary Item can no longer be traded with other players or dropped without destroying it. However, they can still be placed into your STASH.

Best Builds allows players to Submit, Visit, and Rate submitted C.A.M.P.s.   Submitted Best Builds will be populated and shared throughout the Wasteland for all players across all Adventure Mode servers to visit and see.   Submitting Your Camp You can Submit your C.A.M.P. through the Best Builds Submission option. This is found by opening the Paper Map, opening the 'C.A.M.P. Slots' list, and selecting the C.A.M.P. you wish to submit.  Once you have entered the Submission Window, you'll be able to take and add photos and tag your C.A.M.P. with the appropriate identifiers to make it stand out. Once you are happy with how your C.A.M.P. is represented, you can Submit your Best Build.  The Best Build submission will be added to the list of player-created Best Builds and will be populated across the Adventure Mode servers. Once populated, players will be able to visit and 'Like' your Best Build.   If you happen to make changes to your Best Build, you can easily resubmit the C.A.M.P. without losing any previously earned 'Likes'. You can resubmit your Best Build by going to the 'Manage Best Builds' option, also found within the 'C.A.M.P. Slots' list, on the Paper Map.   Visiting a Best Build Populated Best Builds are indicated by a Blue Ribbon around Map Markers in the Paper Map and on the Compass.   These are our player-created Best Builds. You will be able to fast travel to these C.A.M.P.s the same as you would any other C.A.M.P..   While visiting, please take time to sit down, relax, and enjoy the experience the builder has in store for you. Don't delay on checking out a C.A.M.P. that piques your interest; Best Builds are refreshed every hour.   Rating a Best Build If you find a Best Build that you appreciate, you can show your support to the builder by giving them a 'Like'. You can 'Like' a Best Build by going to the Best Build Icon on the Paper Map and selecting 'Like'.   Your 'Likes' help other players identify the best of the Best Builds.

Caravans Escort and defend Brahmin on the perilous Skyline Drive! Travel along one of several predetermined routes, defend cargo from vicious enemies, and deposit it into a box at the end of its path to receive a substantial reward.  Setting Up a Caravan To begin running caravans, visit Stony Man Lookout at level 20 (minimum) and follow the clues to Milepost Zero. Marley will need your help with deliveries. After talking to her and starting a new mission, open the paper map and select your caravan. This can be identified by a Brahmin head icon and your character's name. Clicking it will transport you to the Brahmin, and you can begin your new job. You may run one small caravan for free each hour. If you'd like to run more caravans after your first free one, talk to Marley. She will charge you a gradually decreasing fee and get you set up with a new caravan route.  Supplies Safely delivering your cargo will award you a new currency known as Supplies, as well as various miscellaneous items. Your Supply reward will vary depending on cargo size, which can be adjusted by talking to Marley, but be warned: bigger cargo shipments will lead to a more difficult challenge on the road. Supplies can be used to upgrade Milepost Zero in many exciting ways. Hire new employees, promote them, or talk to them when they arrive at your base to purchase various services.  Multiple Caravans Embark on your own caravan adventure, or join friends to earn Supplies together. A maximum of three caravans can be running on the map at once, but one player can only own one caravan. Any caravans that are already on the road can be seen by opening the paper map.

The Ping System is a player communication tool that allows players to place visual highlights in the world.  Players can use the ping system to highlight actors, objects, interactions and paths for all teammates to see and is greatly beneficial for relaying information in the heat of a battle and for teams without group chats enabled.   Players can place pings into game world by pressing [MOUSE4].   The placed ping is contextual and will change form and color based on the type of object highlighted  Placing a ping in the world will contextually indicate one of the following to all team members:        • Yellow Ping Icon -- Default / No Contextual Target       • Orange Ping Icon -- Containers      • Blue Ping Icon -- Activators      • Red Ping Icon -- Enemy Actor      • Green Ping Icon -- Friendly Actor      • Grey Ping Icon -- Dead Actor   Pings are only visible to teammates in proximity to the player who placed the ping, or who are in the same interior location.  Pings that are off-screen will stick to the edge of the screen in the direction of the ping.

Evade provides a chance to avoid all incoming damage from direct attacks. Evade has a short cooldown based on the damage avoided and cannot happen when over encumbered or while in Power Armor. The cooldown is increased when wearing armor. Medium and Heavy armor have higher cooldown penalties.
Some items and abilities may allow damage to be Reflected. This damage receives bonuses from having a higher armor rating, but is not affected by Perks or other damage modifiers.

Deflect grants a chance to reduce incoming damage from a ranged attack by 50% and reflect 100% of the damage back to the attacker. Deflect chance receives a 50% bonus while wearing 5 pieces of heavy armor or while in Power Armor. While in Power Armor, the amount of damage reflected is doubled too. Explosions cannot be deflected. Bonuses to Reflected Damage also apply to Deflected attacks.

- Represented by a Droplet icon  Poison damage can be dealt by certain plants and animals, especially Insects and mutated creatures, as well as weapons employed by humans for biological warfare.  Corrosive and acidic substances can also deal Poison damage.  - Poison damage is typically paired with a Damage over Time effect which deals additional damage over a long period of time.  Poison damage is most effective against lightly-armored organic targets.  Inorganic enemies such as Robots are often immune to Poison damage.

- Represented by a Lightning Bolt icon  Energy damage is most frequently dealt by Laser and Plasma Weapons, as well as attacks which utilize electricity.  It's also featured in extraterrestrial and otherworldly attacks.  Energy damage is most effective against electronic and metallic enemies such as Robots and Turrets.

Some attacks deal Damage over Time (DoT), meaning the target will continue to lose additional health after the attack impacts the target.  These effects wear off over time and can be resisted by armor, perks, or other effects that reduce damage or provide resistances to the damage type being dealt by the Damage over Time effect.  - Damage over Time effects are represented by a triangular icon under enemy health bars which will indicate the remaining duration for the effect.

- Represented by a Radiation icon  Radiation damage is common in areas that are highly irradiated such as Nuke Zones and storage facilities for nuclear waste.  Some weapons deal Radiation damage such as the Gamma Gun, and Glowing or otherwise mutated enemies may also emit Radiation either passively or when they attack.  - See the "Radiation" Help section for more information  Power Armor, certain consumable items like Rad-X, and Hazmat Suits provide high resistance to Radiation damage.  Radiation damage is most effective against lightly-armored organic targets.  Mutated and irradiated creatures can be highly resistant or even immune to Radiation damage.

- Represented by a Snowflake icon  Cryo damage can be found in advanced weaponry such as the Cryolator as well as specialized modifications for certain weapons.  - Cryo damage is commonly paired with a Slow effect which reduces the speed of the affected target for a short period of time.  Smaller and lightly-armored targets tend to be less resistant to Cryo  damage.  Creatures with thick fur are resistant to Cryo damage.  Robots and other inorganic targets are strongly resistant to Cryo damage.

- Represented by a Shield icon  Physical damage typically occurs from bullets, blunt and sharp melee weapons, and the impact force of most explosions.  Physical damage is the most common form of damage in Appalachia and is reasonably effective against most targets.  Physical damage is most commonly resisted by armored targets such as Robots and Turrets, humans wearing Power Armor, or large creatures with thick hides.

- Represented by a Flame icon  Fire damage can be found from specialized weapons like Flamers and modified weapons which feature incendiary rounds, jets of flame, or heating elements.  Burning objects throughout Appalachia and even some creatures can also deal Fire damage.  - Fire damage is typically paired with a Damage over Time effect which deals additional damage over a short period of time. Feral represents how much sanity you must have to maintain the sense of oneself.  The Feral meter appers in the lower-right corner of the screen, replacing the Hunger and Thirst meter. Feral is represented by a skull crack icon.  If you do not see either meter, you can open the Pip-Boy to bring them up.  You can restore Feral by consuming Chems & Perk Abilities.  The Feral meter drains over time. The meter provides bonuses and penalties depending on how full the meter is:  Feral Meter  - Above 80 percent: you gain +3 Strength,  +3 Endurance, +30 Max HP   - Above 60 percent: you gain +15 Max HP  - Above 40 percent: you lose -1 Endurance and -5 Max AP  - Above 25 percent: you lose -3 Endurance, -15 Max HP, -10 Max AP  - At 0 percent: you gain +150% Melee Damage, and lose -5 Endurance, -30 Max HP, -99 Charisma, -20 Max AP, -300% Hip-fire Gun Accuracy & Range V.A.T.S Accuracy.

Exposure to radiation (or "rads"), causes Glow, increasing your maximum health.  The amount of Glow you've accumulated is displayed in a Green-stripped pattern on your HP bar. Your Pip-Boy also has a built-in radiation indicator on the right of its screen.  You can gain Glow by consuming tainted foods and beverages or being exposed to an irradiated environment. If your Pip-Boy's Geiger counter starts to click, it means you've entered an irradiated area.   The amount of Glow you are currently gaining will be displayed above your HP bar. If you're in Power Armor, your current rad intake will be displayed on the "Rads" dial next to your Hit Points.  You can use Glow for Perk Abilities that increase damage of your weapons, and mitigating any damage taken.  Any item or environment that removes rads will remove Glow instead.

The Level 50 Character Boost increases your active character's level to 50. The Level 50 Character Boost is not available to characters if they are already level 50 or above.  In addition to increasing the character's level, the Level 50 Boost grants the character a Perk Loadout and equipment that are level-appropriate. The Perk Loadout and equipment are automatically equipped to the character. Any Perks or equipment that were previously equipped will still be in the character's Perk Menu or Inventory.  If the character that was boosted is deleted, the Loadout and levels will be lost.

After reaching Level 50, the player unlocks a quest that can transform their Human Character into a Ghoul.  Playing as a Ghoul will introduce new mechanics related to Radiation, Disguising, and allows access to exclusive Perks and Legendary Perks for Ghouls.  Ghouls also will have the following stats applied to them:  -10 Charisma 100% Disease Resist  Select Human Perks will be disabled and unequipped.  Players may turn back their characters into Human through the main menu.  Any perks equipped that are ghoul exclusive will be locked out and unequipped.  Characters in custom worlds cannot revert back to human.

The C.A.M.P. (Construction and Assembly Mobile Platform) allows you to build your own corner of Appalachia in any way you see fit.   Setting up C.A.M.P.  [Pipboy] then [LShoulder] - Open your Pip-Boy then set your C.A.M.P.  The C.A.M.P. will appear in front of you, highlighted in either blue or red. If the highlight is blue,   [Activate] - Place your C.A.M.P.  If the highlight is red, the C.A.M.P. cannot be placed here. It might be too close to an existing location or the ground might not be flat enough. Move around until you find a position where the C.A.M.P. turns blue.  Benefits of the C.A.M.P. Your C.A.M.P. appears on your map as an icon of your choice. Fast traveling to your C.A.M.P. is always free, regardless of how far away it is from you.  One of the most important items you can build at your C.A.M.P. is the Stash Box. A Stash Box can store a large amount of items and is secure against other Players. Only you can see and access your stash.  Moving your C.A.M.P.  You can move your C.A.M.P. to a new location.  [Pipboy] then [LShoulder] - Open your Pip-Boy then move your C.A.M.P.  When you move your C.A.M.P., anything you built at your old site is packed up and placed in the Stored category in the building mode menu.  When you log out from the game, your C.A.M.P. is packed up. When you log back on, the game will try to set up your C.A.M.P. the way you left it.

Alamosaurus roamed North America during the Late Cretaceous period.  Fun Fact: These gigantic herbivores could grow up to 85 feet long and 16 feet tall.
Triceratops were herbivores from the Late Cretaceous period.  Fun Fact: They are named after their distinctive "three-horned faces".

Ancient North America wasn't just shaped by beasts, but by the land itself. Volcanic eruptions, shifting plates, and rising seas created dramatic changes in habitat. Some scientists believe these forces played a role in the Sauropod Hiatus, reshaping the continent and the lives of the creatures who called it home.  Information provided by the North American Paleontology Revival Collective (NAPRC)
Stegosaurus were armored herbivores from the Late Jurassic period.  Fun Fact: While their unique back plates look impressive, scientists are still uncertain what they were used for.
Troodon were small but tenacious hunters from the Late Cretaceous period.  Fun Fact: Some of the earliest discovered dinosaur fossils in America belong to Troodon!
Suuwassea were plant eating sauropods from the Late Jurassic period.  Fun Fact: It is believed that Suuwassea travelled in herds.
Tenontosaurus were large ornithopod herbivores from the Early Cretaceous period.  Fun fact: Tenontosaurus have large tails covered with hard, bony tendons.
Appalachiosaurus were predators native to the Appalachia region in the Late Cretaceous period.  Fun Fact: The Appalachiosaurus is a close relative of the Tyrannosaurus.
Brontosaurus were gigantic herbivores from the Late Jurassic period.  Fun Fact: Brontosaurus means "thunder lizard" because of their massive size.

The discovery of dinosaur eggs provided crucial insight into the reproductive strategies of these ancient creatures. Fossilized eggs, often found in clusters, show us that many species, from the giant sauropods to the small theropods, laid eggs in nests, much like modern-day reptiles and birds.  The most famous of these are the fossilized Maiasaura eggs, which show evidence of parental care. These ancient parents likely stayed with their eggs, protecting and possibly even nurturing the young until they hatched. A behavior that might surprise some, given the image of dinosaurs as brutal, solitary beasts.  Information provided by the North American Paleontology Revival Collective (NAPRC)
