Bounty Hunters needed! Track down targets across Burning Springs and Skyline Valley.  Grunt Hunts You may start a Grunt Hunt at any time for free.  To begin your mission, interact with the stack of contracts at the Last Resort Saloon in Highway Town, or the Trading Post in Skyline Valley.  After getting your target, head to the location specified in your objective and prepare to fight! Killing the target will give you rewards, and you can loot their body for additional items. After all, they won't be needing them, will they?  Head Hunts After completing a few Grunt Hunts, you might receive a Wanted Poster for a powerful Head Hunt target.  If you're itchy trigger finger can't be scratched fast enough, you can buy a Wanted Poster directly from your local Bounty Hunter: the Ghoul in the Last Resort, Burning Springs; Marshal Canton in the Trading Post, Skyline Valley.  After obtaining a poster, pin it on the board near by to inform others that you have started a hunt. You'll find one outside the Saloon, and at the center of the Trading Post.  Your contract will tell you where the target is located. Head Hunts are tough and will often have back-up, so use the flare to alert other Vault Dwellers of their location. Only one Head Hunt can be active at a time, so band together to take down those dastardly outlaws before they can get away.  A successful Head Hunt will give you glory... and a great payout.   Happy hunting!

While exploring the world, you'll come across special objects called "collectibles". These vary in appearance based on the region you're in and the quest they are associated with. Typically, a collectible will be associated with a distinct looping sound effect.  Collectibles are always associated with a quest or special limited time event. Picking up the first collectible in a series will add that quest to your Pip-Boy.  These quests will generally direct you toward a character in the world, or a set of objectives to complete. The more collectibles you find, the further along you'll progress through the story.  In Burning Springs, you can find Abraxodyne Intel Briefcases. In Skyline Valley, you can find mysterious Brain Jars.  During the Limited-time Event, The Slasher, you will find Pint-Sized Slasher masks on unfortunate victims.  Even after completing the quest content associated with the collectibles (which only requires a subset to be found) you can still receive additional rewards via a Challenge, found in your Challenges menu. Try to find all collectibles of the same type for an extra valuable reward.

When a hostile faction seizes control of an area, its usual inhabitants are replaced with powerful and dangerous enemies - led by a highly-challenging faction boss that can drop Four-Star Legendary rewards when defeated.  Infestation events will only occur in outdoor locations within Appalachia, making familiar territory feel dangerous and unpredictable.  Active Infestation Zones will be shown on your map to provide an approximate location -  you'll only know the exact location when you walk right into it... as will your team mates.   Stay sharp out there - in Appalachia, no place stays safe for long.

Seasonal fish are rare fish that appear in specific regions across Appalachia only during certain calendar months. For example, summer fish can only be caught during the months of June through September.  Processing seasonal fish at a cooking station creates special seasonal ingredients used to make powerful cooking recipes.  But remember, once the season changes, the fish will no longer be available until the season returns!  For information on which season is currently active, and where to find the fish, look for a Fishing Report note on Captain Raymond's desk at Fisherman's Rest in the Mire.

Using the Pet Command Wheel, Pets can FOLLOW, STAY, ATTACK and PROTECT.  During FOLLOW and STAY, they won't engage enemies and enemies will ignore them.  In ATTACK they will automatically attack when in combat range. PROTECT means they will wait for the player to take damage before automatically engaging in combat. They are always neutral to other human Players or neutral NPC.  PROTECT is the Pet default stance.  Using the FOLLOW command recalls your Pet instantly if it is far away from you.  Pets can sustain damage and ultimately fall wounded, but they will never die. Use any Stimpak on your injured or wounded Pet to instantly bring them back to full health. By default, it uses the lowest quality Stimpak available in your inventory. If not healed, they will get up with minimal health after combat ends.  In combat, your Pet will target the last pinged enemy. They will also travel to any pinged location when not in combat.

Equipping buffs Once a Pet buff is unlocked, it can be equipped in the Pip-Boy PETS section via the PET BUFFS option. Up to 2 buffs can be simultaneously equipped. Any Pet can use any buffs. Using a different Pet does not change the equipped selection of buffs. Buffs can be manually changed at any time that best fits the situation or your play style.  Unlockable Pet buffs are:  Dog Your Pet finds Stimpaks. Get additional Legendary Item when completing a Grunt Hunt with a Pet.  Cat Your Pet finds Improved Baits. Get Fish Bits when catching a fish with a Pet.  Radhog Your Pet finds Toxic-Goo. Get High-Radiation Fluid in nuke zones with a Pet.  Deathclaw Your Pet finds Black Titanium. Get additional Legendary Item when completing an Infestation with a Pet.

XP and Leveling Pets gain experience points, level-up and earn rewards. Your active Pet banks XP every second (max 1 minute) and collects the banked XP every time you earn XP. Collecting Pet XP from a kill earns your Pet an extra 10 percent Pet XP.  Every day, Pets earn bonus XP for a few hours upon logging and summoning a Pet. The Pet XP Bonus timer resets at the same time as daily challenges and pauses when no Pet is active.  When your Pet has earned enough XP, they will gain levels. At major level milestones, they unlock rewards. You can review the list of milestones and then claim the rewards in the Pet Progression Menu accessible via the Pip-Boy PETS section or the Pet Command Wheel.  Rewards Pets earn many different rewards. The list or rewards for each Pet species are: passive buffs, damage & health upgrades, carry capacity increases, player titles, currencies/consumables and cosmetics/customizations.  Combat upgrades, carry capacity and Pet buffs stats are displayed in the Pip-Boy under STATS/EFFECTS. They each have tiers and can be improved multiple times.

Pets can follow you in the Appalachian. More than that, they can be issued commands, do combat, earn experience points and rewards!  You may acquire Pets in the Atomic Shop. Luckily, there is one available for free!  Pip-Boy  You can manage your Pet in the PETS section of the Pip-Boy, where is displayed the list of Pets you own, their name, their XP Level, their current health and damage stats.   Use the Pip-Boy to activate any of your Pets. They will appear right next to you. Only 1 Pet can be active at a time. Pets can follow you pretty much everywhere, except for Shelters and Raids. If your Pet cannot path to you, no worries. They will automatically find a way to regroup when allowed.  Command Wheel  You can interact with your Pet directly (or through the player emote wheel) to bring up the Pet Command Wheel and give your Pet Commands. This is also where you find the option to rename or customize your Pet.
